speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs regarding the 14 online social media posts which seemingly targeted the Indian community and undermined Singapore's multiculturalism (a) whether investigations have revealed the posts to be a coordinated and deliberate effort by any particular agency or organisation; and (b) if so, what action has been or will be taken against such agency or organisation.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs in view of the Disabling Directions recently issued to block online posts targeting the Indian community (a) whether the Ministry will consider reviewing the current national framework and tools to counteract such external influences; and (b) what upcoming programmes or initiatives are being planned to equip residents with the competencies to discern such negative external influences, whether individually or through community efforts.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The posts attempted to sow discord by inciting ill-will against our Indian community and sought to undermine Singapore’s model of multiculturalism.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The content was assessed to constitute to an offence of knowingly promoting feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different groups on grounds of race and doing acts prejudicial to the maintenance of harmony in Singapore under section 298A(a) of the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In recent years, there has been an increase in artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled and inauthentic content on a range of topics which has seeped into Singapore’s online infospace.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We monitor the infospace closely and will not hesitate to take measures if it is in Singapore’s interests.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The Government regularly reviews our laws to ensure that they are updated and fit for purpose to deal with the evolving landscape.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Aside from the legislative measures, building up a discerning and resilient populace against external influences is equally important.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The Ministry of Defence drives National Education and Total Defence to build a shared understanding of Singapore's foundational values and principles to deepen our public's sense of identity and nationhood, and to strengthen awareness of and collective resolve against threats that may undermine social cohesion and resilience, including foreign interference.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The SG101 website is a one-stop Government site that consolidates educational resources on foreign interference, as well as Singapore's positions on sensitive issues to help the public better understand our national positions and to stay resilient against attempts to divide us.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The National Library Board works to cultivate critical reading as a foundational skill and to engage the public through its Source, Understand, Research, and Evaluate (S.U.R.E) programme, and this equips our citizens with the skills to verify and fact-check online content.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In addition, we regularly conduct briefings, dialogues and workshops to raise awareness of foreign interference amongst groups including our public servants, national servicemen and students.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: This effort will continue, so as to raise awareness of the role that our Singaporeans can play.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Ultimately, a discerning population is the most important defence against attempts to influence or divide our society.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We urge Singaporeans to be discerning when consuming and disseminating information online, and to reject all attempts to divide our society.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We take a serious view of threats to our social cohesion and racial harmony, including external actors, and will act resolutely against them.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While it is heartening to know that there have been no evidence of external influence in this case, I would like to ask if the Government does indeed keep track of possible cases that fuel the possible coordinated efforts of organisations and agencies that may not be made so public and if so, are such cases on the rise?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second question would be, if these cases show evidence also of the influence of state actors, what actions would our Government typically take?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, we do see an increase and we do track very carefully every single case, including investigating whether there are possibly state actors behind the posts.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Some of this information, we may not find that it is suitable to release to the public, but we do look at every single case.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We track the data over time to ensure that there is no coordinated campaign.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: More importantly, we will not hesitate to take action if there is a need to protect Singapore's interests.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Ultimately, we hold the view that any country out there would agree with us that we are just safeguarding our information space.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And if we are interested in protecting our social cohesion – and we are – they will agree with us that such content is unacceptable and that the stance that we have taken is totally understandable.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Our current framework of preventing external influences is primarily based on a couple of Acts or laws: the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act (or FICA), the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) and also OCHA.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: These are, in the view of our population, pretty much reactive in nature.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The population looks at it as what we do after the events have happened.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The question is, how effective are they and how do we measure this effectiveness?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Is the Ministry exploring more preventive measures compared to these slightly more reactive measures?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: What are the programmes or initiatives that are preventive in nature and again, how effective are they?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Specifically, how to educate or train or inoculate our residents from believing or disseminating such malicious influence?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Mr Speaker, allow me to reiterate my response to the Members' questions.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The Government had to act decisively against these videos because they seek to undermine Singapore's cohesion, and they seek to attack our multi-racial society and attempt to divide us based on our race.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Our societal harmony cannot be taken for granted because it has been painstakingly developed over decades and every community in Singapore is valued.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: This diversity in Singapore's fabric is our greatest strength, but it requires deliberate and constant protection against division.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: These videos strike at the very foundation of what makes Singapore home for all of us.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: That is why the Government acted firmly against these videos, especially also because they originated from a foreign source.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We must reject all attempts that seek to divide us.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: He also mentioned that we do have various Acts in place.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Yes, I would like to reiterate that the Government has various legislative levers, some more recently introduced, in place to deal with such threats.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: These include FICA, the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act, POFMA, as well as OCHA.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: These are a range of levers that allow us to be able to act decisively should any such narrative or attempt to divide us arise.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I want to make the point that having these laws allows us to be very proactive, going upstream to demonstrate that we not only have the laws and that we are also willing to exercise these laws to protect our citizens and our social fabric before our racial harmony is affected.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In my main reply earlier, I have also listed various efforts in terms of public education.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Every incident that has happened is also a potential learning opportunity that we will use to educate our public to fight such division efforts.
